sasha: heads-up — saw sharp p95 spikes yesterday evening when host-pool C started backfilling to cheaper instances.
aj: is this the same backfill behavior that slid traffic to the micro-gpus? did admission already try reserve tokens first?
sasha: yes. admission fell back but our current backfill policy just floods the next tier; small instances got overloaded and latency spiked.
kevin: quick thought — prefer a capacity-preserving backfill: only let a small % of requests spill per-tenant so we don't thrash small pools.
maria: interface question — who owns the decision? runtime detects pressure, scheduler/admission should make the final choice. do we need a new RPC or enrich existing request headers?
leo: we could add a lightweight BackfillRecommendation proto: priority_hint, max_spill_pct, latency_target_ms. runtime emits it when it detects graceful degradation.
aj: want to avoid tight coupling between runtime and admission. make the proto optional and keep existing "preferred_variant" header as a fallback.
sasha: we'll also need telemetry: per-tenant spill_rate, observed_latency_ms, and backfill_failover_count so we can detect regressions.
maria: ops wants an alert: spill_rate > 5% && p95_latency > SLO for 5m -> page. can we start with a conservative threshold?
kevin: tradeoffs: more signals let us make smarter choices but increase instability surface. recommended default max_spill_pct = 3% and a 30s cool-down window.
leo: propose experiment plan: canary 1% traffic with backfill_recommendation honored, measure p95 latency, fairness-score delta, and cost delta over 72h.
aj: neat. action items: leo -> Proto PR; sasha -> telemetry hooks + local sim; maria -> alert recipe + PagerDuty runbook; kevin -> experiment dashboard.
sasha: I'll stub the metrics today and add a minimal dashboard. tagging @eng-platform for rollout coordination. :+1:
kevin: timeline check — aim to have PRs and a canary by EOW? if anyone needs more runway call it out now.
maria: EOW sounds ok for initial canary signoff. thanks y'all.
